en: Auspicious morning to Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa.
Auspicious Dawn to Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa.
Now begins the *Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa Suprabhātam*.
"O Rāma, Kausalyā is a mother of noble offspring; the morning twilight is now dawning.
Arise, O tiger among men; the daily rites for the gods must be performed.
"Arise, arise, O Govinda! Arise, O you whose banner is Garuḍa!"
Arise, O Beloved of Kamalā; bring auspiciousness to the three worlds!
O Mother of all the worlds, you who sport upon the chest of Madhu-Kaiṭabha’s enemy, you of enchanting divine form!
O Śrī Svāminī, whose nature is to grant what is dear to those who take refuge in you, O beloved of Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa—may there be a beautiful dawn for you!
3. May there be a beautiful dawn for you, O lotus-eyed one!
May it be so, O you whose face is like a serene orb of the moon,
who are worshipped by Brahmā, Śiva, Indra, and their consorts,
beloved of the Lord of the Vṛṣa-mountain (Śiva), and treasure-house of compassion! 4.
The seven sages, Atri and the others, having performed their twilight devotions,
approached to worship his two feet, taking with them the enchanting lotuses from the celestial river.
O Lord who crowns Śeṣādri, may you have a beautiful dawn!
The gods, beginning with Pañcānana, Abjabhava, Ṣaṇmukha, and Vāsava, praise your deeds such as the Traivikrama and others.
The Lord of Speech recites from afar the purity of the day: "O Lord who wears the Śeṣa mountain as a crest-jewel, may there be a beautiful dawn for you!
[With] slightly blossoming lotuses and coconuts..."

O Lord who dwells upon the crest of the Śeṣa mountain, may there be a beautiful dawn for you, as a gentle breeze blows along with divine fragrances from the charming flower-baskets of the betel-nut trees and others.
Opening their pair of eyes while perched in their excellent cages,
the pet parrots playfully eat the plantains, milk-rice, and other foods remaining in their bowls, and then recite verses.
O Lord who crowns the Śeṣa mountain, may there be a beautiful dawn for you;
even Nārada sings of your infinite deeds upon the lute, which is sweet-sounding with its excellence of strings.
O Lord who crowns the Śeṣa mountain, may your beautiful dawn be auspicious— a dawn filled with the constant, melodious sounds of birds and delightful with the movements of your hands.
And may the swarm of bees, permeated by the essence of nectar, [attend upon you].
O Lord who crowns the Śeṣa mountain, may there be a beautiful dawn for you, as the bees emerge from the hearts of the lotuses in the nearby lakes to attend upon you with their humming songs.
In the cowherd settlements, while the curds were being churned by groups of women, the loud sounds of the churning produced by the curds caused the earthen jars to emit a harsh,
discordant noise out of anger toward the quarters of the sky.
O Lord who crowns Śeṣādri, may there be a beautiful dawn for you!
O friend of the lotus-lord, the swarms of bees residing upon your hundred-petaled lotus-like feet seek to steal the splendor of the blue water-lily with the beauty of their own limbs.
O Lord who crowns the mountain of Śeṣa, may there be a beautiful dawn for you, who bear a piercing roar like the sound of a kettledrum;
O glorious one, desired by all, the giver of boons, and the kinsman of the entire world.
O Śrī Śrīnivāsa, sole ocean of compassion for the entire world,
O divine form dwelling within the arms of the Goddess,
O Lord of the glorious Veṅkaṭācala— may there be a beautiful dawn for you! 13.
Those whose limbs are purified by bathing in the Śrī Svāmipuṣkariṇī— the Lord Hara, the Creator Viriñca, Sanandana, and others seeking the highest good—
dwell at the gateway with their heads struck by excellent weapons.
O Lord of Śrī Veṅkaṭācala, may there be a beautiful dawn for you.
O Śrī Śeṣaśaila, Garuḍācala, Veṅkaṭādri,
Nārāyaṇādri, Vṛṣabhādri, Vṛṣādri, and foremost of all!

O Lord of the illustrious Veṅkaṭācala, may there be a glorious dawn for you, as the guardians of the quarters— the Rakshasa, Varuṇa, Pavamāna, and Kubera— stand with palms joined in reverence, their own heads shining brightly. 16.

O King of Birds, O Sovereign of Beasts, O Sovereign of Nagas, O King of Elephants, and O Sovereign of Horses, upon the ridges of this mountain you each aspire to the greatness of your respective offices; O Lord of Sri Venkatachala, may there be a glorious dawn for You!
[And likewise for] Surya, Indu, Bhauma, Budha, Vakpati, Kavya, and Sauri... 17.

O Lord of Śrī Veṅkaṭācala, may there be a beautiful dawn for you— whose attendants include Svarbhānu, Ketu, and the foremost of the celestial hosts, and whose servants are the servants of your servants down to the very last. 18.
With their heads throbbing as they are filled with the dust of your feet,
those whose inner hearts are indifferent to heaven and liberation fall into agitation by calculating the arrival of the end of the aeon.
O Lord of Śrī Veṅkaṭācala, may there be a beautiful dawn for you!
Beholding the peaks at the tops of your gopuras,
people take refuge in the supreme path leading to heaven and liberation.

O Lord of Śrī Veṅkaṭācala, mortals in the world of men take refuge in Your thought; may there be a beautiful dawn for You, O Lord of Śrī and Bhūmi, ocean of the nectar of virtues such as compassion! 20.
O God of gods, embodiment of the world’s sole refuge,
O illustrious Ananta, whose feet are worshipped by Garuḍa and others—
O Lord of Śrī Veṅkaṭācala, may there be a beautiful dawn for you! 21.
O Śrī Padmanābha, Puruṣottama, Vāsudeva, Vaikuṇṭha, Mādhava, Janārdana, wielder of the discus!
O you who bear the Śrīvatsa mark, the celestial tree for those who have come for refuge!
O Lord of Śrī Veṅkaṭācala, may you have a glorious dawn!
O beautiful one who shatters the pride of Kandarpa, O divine-formed one whose restless glance rests upon the lotus-buds of your beloved’s breasts!
O Lord of Śrī Veṅkaṭācala, you who are a mine of auspicious and stainless virtues, you of divine fame— may there be a beautiful dawn for you,
O you who take the forms of the Fish, the Tortoise, the Boar, Nṛsiṃha, and the Dwarf! 23.
O Lord, O Rāmacandra whose wealth is asceticism,
O Rāma who is a portion of Śeṣa, O delighter of the Yadus, O you in the form of Kalki,
O Lord of the illustrious Veṅkaṭācala— may there be a beautiful dawn for you! 24
Holding golden jars filled with divine water from sacred fords, fragrant with cardamom, cloves,
and camphor, the foremost jewels of the Vedic tradition were filled with joy.
O Lord of Veṅkaṭa, may there be a beautiful dawn for you! The sun rises, the lotuses bloom,
and the birds fill the quarters with their songs.
O Veṅkaṭa, may there be a beautiful dawn for you, by which the Śrīvaiṣṇavas— who constantly seek auspiciousness— take refuge in your abode,
as do Brahmā and the other foremost gods along with the great sages.
O Lord of Śrī Veṅkaṭācala, may there be a beautiful dawn for you, whose hands hold auspicious objects near your abode, and who are the supreme among yogis with faces that delight the virtuous. 27.

O abode of Lakṣmī, sole ocean of faultless virtues, the unique bridge for crossing the ocean of saṃsāra; O You whose innate majesty is known through the Vedānta, the object of enjoyment for Your devotees!
"O Lord of Śrī Veṅkaṭācala, may there be a beautiful dawn for you.
Those men who here daily engage in reciting this "Beautiful Dawn" (suprabhāta) hymn to the Lord of Vṛṣācala [attain their goal].
At the time of dawn, for those who have partaken in this [prayer], it generates supreme wisdom that easily accomplishes the welfare of others.
Thus ends the *Veṅkaṭeśa-suprabhātam*.
